newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on arbitrage play.

text.p: * Banks to take advantage of long holiday
The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.245 to the dollar on Wednesday from 26.253 as banks shorted their dollars on interest arbitrage play.

"Most banks prefer to be short on dollars," said a dealer, so they could have pesos that earn higher interest versus the dollar for the long holiday. Banks' foreign exchange operations will be closed on November 22 and 25 on account of the summit meeting of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).
The peso was more attractive to hold considering the tightness in the money market which had a higher average rate of 13.03125 percent from 12.5625, a foreign bank trader said.
Traders said banks are likely going to buy back on Thursday the dollars they shorted for delivery next Tuesday.
This will set the scenario for a lower peso which would be pulled down by the four-day swap points taking into account the interest premium of the peso over the dollar, dealers said.
After opening at its day-low of 26.250, the peso steadily rose to 26.236, prompting the Central Bank to buy about $112 million at 26.238 to 26.246, a dealer said.
The day's average was at 26.242 versus 26.255 on Tuesday. Volume increased to $209.80 million from $202.90 million.
